front: TC023: What is the minimum viable move?
back: When you cannot answer properly on the spot, say: 'I cannot give you the right answer now — I can have it for you by [specific time].' Then keep that commitment.

front: TC023: What is the core sequence?
back: Decline to decide now -> Specific return time -> Honour the commitment.

front: TC023: What is the field tip?
back: The specific time is the whole technique.

front: TC023: What is the strong version of: Vague deferral: 'I will let you know...'?
back: I cannot give you the right answer now. I will come back to you by [specific time].

front: TC023: What is the strong version of: Endless deferral with no committed return?
back: Specific time commitment made and kept.

front: TC023: What is the strong version of: Provisional answer presented as final?
back: Provisionally yes — I will confirm by X.

front: TC023: What is better than: 'Let me think about it and I will get back to you.'?
back: 'Let me think about it — I will come back to you by Wednesday morning.'

front: TC023: What is better than: (Thursday arrives; you say nothing and hope they forgot)?
back: 'I promised you an answer today and I need one more day. Tomorrow, guaranteed.'

front: TC023: What is better than: 'I need a bit more time on this...' — days after you decided?
back: 'I have thought about it, and the honest answer is no.'

front: TC023: What are signs it is working?
back: You return with answers on the timelines you commit to. People accept the deferral because they trust the deadline. Your answer, when it comes, is better than the one you would have given on the spot. Deferrals are occasional — not habitual.

front: TC023: When should you avoid this technique?
back: When you know the answer already — deferring when you could decide now signals avoidance. When the other person needs an answer urgently and deferment will cause real harm or delay.

front: TC023: What is the best recovery line?
back: 'I gave you an answer on the spot that I should have slept on. Can I revise it?'
